# SK2051 — The arithmetic has a result its constant operand already fixes

<!-- Generated from Rules/Rikarin.Skala.Rules.Metadata/rules.json. Do not edit. -->

A built-in integral arithmetic or bitwise operation has a constant operand that makes the operation either the identity or a constant.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | Correctness |
| Default severity | warning |
| Scope | Semantic |
| Needs a compilation | yes |
| Fix | yes, safe |
| Language version floor | — |
| Since | 1.3 |
| ReSharper | `UselessBinaryOperation` (`resharper_useless_binary_operation_highlighting`) |

## Why

`x * 1`, `x | 0` and `x & 0` compute nothing. Written by hand they are usually the residue of an edit that removed the interesting operand, and written by a model they are usually a placeholder that was never filled in — which is why the range matters more for generated code than for code somebody typed. ⚠ Every case reported here holds identically in a checked and an unchecked context: an identity cannot overflow and a constant result cannot either, so the project's CheckForOverflowUnderflow setting never changes the answer.

## Example

Instead of:

```csharp
var scaled = weight * 1;
```

Write:

```csharp
var scaled = weight;
```

## When it does not fire

Only built-in, non-lifted `+ - * / % & | ^` whose result type is a fixed-width integral type is considered, and the non-constant operand's type must equal that result type — so `someByte * 1` is left alone, because removing the operator would change the expression's static type and a `var` target with it. ⚠ Floating point is excluded on purpose: `x + 0.0` is not the identity, because it turns negative zero into positive zero. `0 - x` is negation, not an identity, and is not reported. Where the operation has a constant result rather than an identity — `x & 0`, `x % 1`, `x | -1` — the other operand must be a plain local, parameter or non-volatile field reference, so that discarding its evaluation cannot discard a side effect; anything else is left alone rather than reported without a fix. Compound assignment (`x *= 1`), shifts (which SK2052 owns), enums, pointers, decimal, `Math.Clamp` with an inverted range and cross-file constant dependencies are all outside this initial scope.

## Configuration

- `dotnet_diagnostic.SK2051.severity`
